summary: Arduino Uno SMD shows global 5V (0.4V) and 3.3V (0.1V) rail collapse on both USB and DC inputs with ON LED dark and no enumeration. Pattern indicates common downstream short/overload on 5V rail dragging both supplies into current-limit, not an upstream open. Primary suspects: shorted 5V rail load, shorted 3.3V regulator/rail reflecting to 5V, or failed NCP1117 5V regulator.

visibleObservations.description: No obvious smoke, charring, or burnt substrate visible on top side at this resolution
visibleObservations.evidence: Blue PCB top view, angled; area near DC jack, NCP1117 regulator, C1/C2 electrolytics, USB-B jack shows no discoloration

visibleObservations.description: Key power path landmarks identifiable but fine solder detail not resolvable
visibleObservations.evidence: USB-B jack left edge, DC barrel jack bottom edge, two 47uF electrolytics near NCP1117ST50T3G, ATmega328P SMD and ATmega16U2 present, F1 polyfuse and D1 diode area near USB/DC

visibleObservations.description: ON and L LEDs appear off, consistent with reported unpowered/collapsed rail state
visibleObservations.evidence: Photo shows board unpowered; no illumination visible near ON silkscreen and pin 13 L area

hypotheses.title: Dead short on 5V rail overloading F1 polyfuse and NCP1117 regulator
hypotheses.reasoning: 0.4V on 5V from both USB (via F1) and DC (via D1->NCP1117) implies common load short to GND pulling supplies into current limit/foldback. ON LED (5V-powered) dark supports this.
supportingEvidence: Technician disconnected quickly to avoid thermal runaway suggesting high current
hypotheses.suggestedVerification: Unpowered cold resistance 5V to GND at 5V header pin; healthy >1kΩ, short <10Ω indicates rail short. Then isolate by checking 3.3V regulator input resistance and downstream ICs.

hypotheses.title: Shorted LP2985-33 3.3V regulator or 3.3V rail short dragging 5V down
hypotheses.reasoning: LP2985-33 input is fed from 5V rail. Internal VIN-GND short or output short with pass element failure will load 5V heavily, causing 5V to collapse to 0.4V and 3.3V to 0.1V.
supportingEvidence: U1 regulator section flagged as suspect
hypotheses.suggestedVerification: Unpowered resistance 3.3V to GND and 5V to 3.3V regulator VIN pin to GND; compare to known-good. Lift/desolder LP2985 input if short confirmed to see if 5V recovers.

hypotheses.title: Failed NCP1117ST50T3G 5V regulator internally shorted or D1/F1 degraded after overvoltage/reverse event
hypotheses.reasoning: Shorted NCP1117 (VIN-GND or VOUT-GND) will clamp Vin and hold 5V low on DC input; if 5V rail also shorted, USB via F1 also collapses. Tripped polyfuse F1 or open D1 alone would not explain both inputs failing simultaneously unless accompanied by downstream short.
supportingEvidence: Failure on both USB and DC paths
No visible damage - internal semiconductor short possible
Suspect components include D1, F1, U1 near DC jack
hypotheses.suggestedVerification: Unpowered diode-mode check D1 (should be ~0.3-0.7V one way), F1 resistance (<1Ω cold, high if tripped/open), NCP1117 VIN-GND and VOUT-GND resistance/diode check for shorts.

recommendedChecks.title: Unpowered visual inspection and cold rail resistance
recommendedChecks.procedure: With USB and DC disconnected, inspect under magnification: F1, D1, NCP1117, LP2985, C1/C2, USB-B pins, ATmega328P/16U2 for cracks, solder bridges, flux residue, bulged caps. Then measure resistance 5V header to GND and 3.3V header to GND. Also measure VIN to GND.
recommendedChecks.expectedResult: No burnt/cracked parts. 5V-GND >1kΩ (often 3-10kΩ), 3.3V-GND >500Ω, VIN-GND >10kΩ. <10-50Ω indicates hard short.
safetyNotes: Keep board fully unpowered and disconnected from USB/host

recommendedChecks.title: Unpowered continuity of polyfuse F1, diode D1, and regulators
recommendedChecks.procedure: Measure F1 across terminals: should be <1-5Ω cold (polyfuse). Measure D1 anode-cathode diode drop: ~0.4-0.7V forward, OL reverse. Measure NCP1117 VIN-VOUT-GND and LP2985 VIN-VOUT-GND for shorts (diode mode). Check USB-B 5V pin to F1 to 5V rail continuity.
recommendedChecks.expectedResult: F1 low resistance, D1 rectifying, no regulator pin shorted to GND (<0.1V diode drop both directions indicates short).
safetyNotes: Do not apply external power during continuity tests

recommendedChecks.title: Current-limited power injection to locate short (thermal/voltage)
recommendedChecks.procedure: Set lab supply to 5V, current limit 100mA, inject at 5V header GND/5V (disconnect USB/DC). Monitor voltage and current; if current hits limit at ~0.4V, short confirmed. Use thermal camera or alcohol evaporation to find hottest component (regulator, cap, MCU). If no heat, lift LP2985 input to isolate 3.3V rail.
recommendedChecks.expectedResult: Healthy board draws 30-80mA at 5V with 5V stable. Shorted board hits 100mA limit with voltage collapse and one component heats rapidly.
safetyNotes: Never exceed 5.5V or 200mA limit to avoid PCB trace damage
Do not probe mains-powered DC adapter

limitations: Single angled top-view photo, low resolution; solder joints, component markings (U1, D1, F1), and bottom-side traces not visible
No powered thermal/IR or high-res close-up of regulator/capacitor area to confirm shorts
Cannot verify prior overvoltage, reverse polarity, or ESD event history that could explain simultaneous rail collapse
safetyWarnings: Do not touch energized regulator, polyfuse, or capacitors; risk of burns from thermal runaway
Use current-limited supply only; unregulated 9V DC jack can source high current into short
Observe ESD precautions for ATmega328P/16U2 CMOS devices
